`HANDOFF.md` step 0.

## Expected behavior

GitHub is the ordinary issue and PR surface for track A. The lifecycle tools use
`gh` to create and update GitHub issues and pull requests, post local CI commit
statuses, and post local review verdicts. The committed local registry remains a
complete write-through record and permits work to continue during transient link,
CLI, or authentication failures.

The integration must be retry-hardened, idempotent under a retry after an
ambiguous failure, and explicit about unsynchronized operations. It must never
turn a missing `gh`, missing authentication, or network outage into silent success.
The local merge gate remains authoritative for CI/review eligibility and must not
push or merge a head that has not passed that gate.

## Scope

- Adapt `issue_new.py` and `issue_close.py` to create/close GitHub issues while
  preserving atomic local records and parent/child bookkeeping.
- Adapt `pr_open.py` and `pr_merge.py` to publish branches and create/update the
  corresponding GitHub pull requests without weakening the local gate.
- Have `ci.sh` post a commit status for the exact checked head SHA.
- Have `review.sh` publish the exact-head review verdict and findings to the
  corresponding GitHub PR.
- Make `github-sync.sh` a retry-hardened push for the standalone repository.
- Add shared configuration, retry, idempotency, and offline-fallback machinery
  rather than duplicating shell fragments across entry points.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, the affected protocol
  documents, and `EVOLUTION.md` so the normative text matches enforcement.
- Add deterministic tests using a fake `gh`; tests must not mutate GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- Online create/update paths are demonstrated against a fake `gh`, including
  local-to-GitHub number mapping and repeated invocation after ambiguous failure.
- Offline and unauthenticated paths preserve a usable local record, emit an
  actionable warning, and retain enough state for an explicit retry/reconciliation.
- CI and review publication is bound to the same head SHA as the local manifest
  and verdict; stale-head publication is rejected.
- Merge remains impossible without green same-head local CI and an acceptable
  same-head local review.
- Existing migrated records use the seed mapping without creating duplicates.
- The issue tree and script tests pass, and no workflow test performs a real

# Brief: GitHub-native workflow without a local issue/PR registry

GitHub issue: `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A#6`

Branch: `issue-0007-github-native-workflow`

Expected PR title: `feat(local): make GitHub the workflow authority`

## Authority

This brief records the owner's 2026-08-31 directive, which supersedes the
earlier write-through/offline-fallback design archived with the old registry.
GitHub is the single source of truth for active issues and pull requests. There
must be no active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, shadow record, write-through cache,
operation journal, or offline mutation mode.

The archive-only commit `c8f1999` moved the former trees verbatim to:

- `results/telemetry/registry-archive/issues/`
- `results/telemetry/registry-archive/prs/`

Those 60 archived files are append-only research data. Do not edit, regenerate,
normalize, or use them as active workflow input.

Session, build, stage, incident, and evolution telemetry remain active and
unchanged. In particular, `dispatch.sh`, `telemetry.py`,
`results/telemetry/{sessions,builds,stages}.jsonl`, and the
`events.md` -> `EVOLUTION.md` amendment pipeline are not registry machinery.

## Shared GitHub layer

Provide one shared Python layer under `local/bin/` for repository discovery,
`gh` execution, JSON parsing, pagination, retry classification, and API
version headers. All lifecycle tools must use it.

- Resolve the CLI from `MIPSTARRE_GH`, then `PATH`, then the documented
  user-local location. Tests set `MIPSTARRE_GH` to a fake executable.
- Resolve the repository from `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` or the `github` remote;
  the documented repository is `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`.
- Probe authentication with a harmless API request. Do not trust
  `gh auth status`, because installed `gh 2.4.0` misreports the valid
  fine-grained PAT.
- Never log a token or pass one on the command line.
- Retry connection failures, timeouts, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx with a bounded
  exponential delay. Do not retry permanent 4xx responses blindly.
- Mutations are online-required. Exhausted or permanent failures return
  nonzero; there is no local success or pending record to fall back to.
- Make ambiguous creates and publications idempotent with stable hidden
  markers and authoritative paginated reads before another write. This is a
  remote retry defense, not a local registry.
- Use `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and a supported explicit GitHub API
  version for REST calls.

## Issue lifecycle

Rewrite `issue_new.py` as a GitHub issue creator and `issue_close.py` as a
GitHub issue closer.

- GitHub issue numbers are the only active issue identifiers. Do not allocate
  zero-padded local ids or write Markdown records.
- `issue_new.py` uses noninteractive `gh issue create`, prints the created or
  adopted issue number and URL, and supports title, body/body-file, labels,
  assignees, and an optional GitHub parent issue number.
- A stable marker in the issue body makes retry after an ambiguous create
  recover the existing issue rather than duplicate it.
- For `--parent`, resolve the child's numeric database id and call
  `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`. GitHub's one-parent
  relation replaces all parent/children frontmatter and tracking counters.
- `issue_close.py` operates on a GitHub number. Map `completed` and
  `not-planned` to GitHub's `state_reason` values and preserve an optional
  explanatory comment.
- Labels come from the repository. Remove `local/labels.yml` as an authority;
  scripts may validate requested labels against the paginated GitHub label
  list and must report a missing label clearly.

## Pull-request lifecycle

Rewrite `pr_open.py` to publish an explicit feature ref and invoke
noninteractive `gh pr create`.

- GitHub PR numbers are the only active PR identifiers.
- Inputs are branch, base, title, body/body-file, labels, and an optional
  closing issue number. Use GitHub-number footers directly.
- Push only `refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>` to the `github` remote.
  Never use `git push --all` and never advance `main` outside the merge path.
- Repeated invocation adopts or updates the unique open PR for the same head
  branch. A branch with no commits ahead of base fails clearly; do not create a
  placeholder commit.
- Keep branch-name safety checks, but future names embed GitHub issue numbers.
  The current migration branch retains its historical local id and closes
  GitHub issue `#6`.

## CI publication

Rewrite `ci.sh` to accept a GitHub PR number and obtain base ref, head ref, and
head SHA from GitHub. Resolve the corresponding local worktree and require its
branch tip to equal the remote PR head before starting.

- Preserve the existing deterministic step commands and change gating.
- For every complete run, publish a status for every gate step on the exact
  starting SHA using context `local-ci/<step>`. Publish `pending` before a step
  and one of `success`, `failure`, or `error` afterward. A non-applicable step
  is a successful status whose description says it was skipped.
- Debug/partial runs must not publish a gate-satisfying status set.
- Re-read both the local branch tip and remote PR head before final
  publication. If either moved, publish no stale success and return nonzero.
- Build the existing manifest schema in runtime storage, then post the full
  JSON as an idempotent PR comment with exact PR/head/run markers. It is not
  written to an active repository registry.
- Keep build telemetry exactly as it is today.

The merge gate requires the latest status for every canonical
`local-ci/<step>` context on the current PR head to be `success`. It must not
trust GitHub's combined status alone, because unrelated contexts may be absent.

## Review publication

Rewrite `review.sh` to accept a GitHub PR number, verify the exact-head CI
statuses, and run the existing trusted-prompt code/prose review lanes.

- Reviewer output lives in runtime storage until the trusted wrapper combines
  it. Do not recreate `prs/<id>/reviews/`.
- Preserve the findings-ledger format in the submitted review body, including
  path/line references and unresolved findings.
- Re-read local and remote head SHAs after reviewers finish. A moved head makes
  the result stale and forbids publication.
- Submit one review bound to `commit_id`, with a stable marker so retry does
  not duplicate an identical review. Use `REQUEST_CHANGES` for unresolved
  findings when GitHub accepts it and `COMMENT` for a clean verdict. Never
  require the PR author's impossible self-approval.
- Publish a separate exact-head `local-review/summary` commit status:
  `success` for an acceptable local verdict and `failure` for unresolved
  findings. This status plus the marker-bound ledger, not a GitHub
  `APPROVED` actor, is the review gate evidence.

## Auto-fix and merge gate

Remove all reads and writes of `pr.md`, local CI manifests, and local verdict
files from `autofix.sh` and `pr_merge.py`.

- Resolve PR branch/base/head and labels from GitHub.
- Preserve the machine-local per-branch fix lock and supersession behavior.
- Derive the combined fix iteration count from PR commits whose subjects begin
  exactly `[codex-auto-fix]` or `[codex-review-fix]`; enforce the configured
  cap from that GitHub-visible history.
- Use a GitHub label for auto-fix opt-in. At the cap, remove the label and post
  a clear PR comment.
- `pr_merge.py` must enforce, in order: open/non-draft/mergeable PR; actual
  local branch tip equals GitHub head; every canonical per-step status is
  successful on that head; review state is acceptable on that same commit;
  no live fix lock; fix iteration count is within cap; and a final head recheck.
- Normal review requires a successful exact-head `local-review/summary` status
  and the matching marker-bound ledger with no unresolved finding. A later
  exact-head `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review still blocks.
- With `--adjudicated`, require a current-head PR comment beginning
  `ADJUDICATION`, containing the findings disposition and stable head marker,
  plus the repository's adjudication label. Missing or stale evidence blocks.
- Merge with modern `gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <sha>`. Probe that
  capability and fail closed on an older CLI. Do not use `--admin`, auto-merge,
  a direct push to `main`, or an unguarded merge.
- After GitHub reports the PR merged, fetch and fast-forward the trusted local
  `main` checkout to the remote merge commit; then remove the local feature
  worktree/branch under the existing cleanup safeguards.

## Local Operations

This repository executes its workflow locally while GitHub holds active issue
and PR state. The short version every agent must know:

- **Build reuse.** A hot main cache lives under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`;
  fresh worktrees get it via `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` (which also
  installs git hooks and resets dirty vendored packages). Never run
  `lake update`; never write to the cache; at most one full `lake build`
  runs machine-wide (the scripts take the lock for you).
- **Lifecycle.** GitHub issue → `issue-N-slug` branch + worktree → agent
  sessions → exact-head `local/bin/ci.sh <pr>` → `local/bin/review.sh <pr>` →
  optional auto-fix → guarded GitHub merge. Active tools use
  `local/bin/github_api.py`; snapshots and the archived registry are never
  lifecycle input. Details: `local/README.md`.
- **Sessions.** Dispatch, resume, and archive agent sessions only via
  `local/bin/dispatch.sh` (roles: orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier,
  blueprint, splitter, scout) so token/time telemetry stays complete.
- **Telemetry duty.** Incidents go to `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  protocol changes follow `local/protocols/meta.md` and are ledgered in
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- **Fix commits** are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]`
  exactly; issue titles, slugs, and branch names stay bracket-free.

## Current behavior

The local lifecycle scripts create and mutate only the committed registries under
`issues/` and `prs/`. Local CI and review record their conclusions only in PR
frontmatter and per-head artifacts. The repository has moved to the standalone
`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A` GitHub repository, but the operative scripts and normative
protocols still describe a local-only surface.

The migration seed maps local issues `#0001`, `#0004`, `#0005`, and `#0006` to
GitHub issues `#1` through `#4`, and local PR `#0003` to GitHub PR `#5`; see
`results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md`. The owner decision is recorded in the
2026-08-31 re-hybridization entry of `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` and in
`HANDOFF.md` step 0.

## Expected behavior

GitHub is the ordinary issue and PR surface for track A. The lifecycle tools use
`gh` to create and update GitHub issues and pull requests, post local CI commit
statuses, and post local review verdicts. The committed local registry remains a
complete write-through record and permits work to continue during transient link,
CLI, or authentication failures.

The integration must be retry-hardened, idempotent under a retry after an
ambiguous failure, and explicit about unsynchronized operations. It must never
turn a missing `gh`, missing authentication, or network outage into silent success.
The local merge gate remains authoritative for CI/review eligibility and must not
push or merge a head that has not passed that gate.

## Scope

- Adapt `issue_new.py` and `issue_close.py` to create/close GitHub issues while
  preserving atomic local records and parent/child bookkeeping.
- Adapt `pr_open.py` and `pr_merge.py` to publish branches and create/update the
  corresponding GitHub pull requests without weakening the local gate.
- Have `ci.sh` post a commit status for the exact checked head SHA.
- Have `review.sh` publish the exact-head review verdict and findings to the
  corresponding GitHub PR.
- Make `github-sync.sh` a retry-hardened push for the standalone repository.
- Add shared configuration, retry, idempotency, and offline-fallback machinery
  rather than duplicating shell fragments across entry points.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, the affected protocol
  documents, and `EVOLUTION.md` so the normative text matches enforcement.
- Add deterministic tests using a fake `gh`; tests must not mutate GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- Online create/update paths are demonstrated against a fake `gh`, including
  local-to-GitHub number mapping and repeated invocation after ambiguous failure.
- Offline and unauthenticated paths preserve a usable local record, emit an
  actionable warning, and retain enough state for an explicit retry/reconciliation.
- CI and review publication is bound to the same head SHA as the local manifest
  and verdict; stale-head publication is rejected.
- Merge remains impossible without green same-head local CI and an acceptable
  same-head local review.
- Existing migrated records use the seed mapping without creating duplicates.
- The issue tree and script tests pass, and no workflow test performs a real
  network mutation.

## Current behavior

The local lifecycle scripts create and mutate only the committed registries under
`issues/` and `prs/`. Local CI and review record their conclusions only in PR
frontmatter and per-head artifacts. The repository has moved to the standalone
`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A` GitHub repository, but the operative scripts and normative
protocols still describe a local-only surface.

The migration seed maps local issues `#0001`, `#0004`, `#0005`, and `#0006` to
GitHub issues `#1` through `#4`, and local PR `#0003` to GitHub PR `#5`; see
`results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md`. The owner decision is recorded in the
2026-08-31 re-hybridization entry of `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` and in
`HANDOFF.md` step 0.

## Expected behavior

GitHub is the ordinary issue and PR surface for track A. The lifecycle tools use
`gh` to create and update GitHub issues and pull requests, post local CI commit
statuses, and post local review verdicts. The committed local registry remains a
complete write-through record and permits work to continue during transient link,
CLI, or authentication failures.

The integration must be retry-hardened, idempotent under a retry after an
ambiguous failure, and explicit about unsynchronized operations. It must never
turn a missing `gh`, missing authentication, or network outage into silent success.
The local merge gate remains authoritative for CI/review eligibility and must not
push or merge a head that has not passed that gate.

## Scope

- Adapt `issue_new.py` and `issue_close.py` to create/close GitHub issues while
  preserving atomic local records and parent/child bookkeeping.
- Adapt `pr_open.py` and `pr_merge.py` to publish branches and create/update the
  corresponding GitHub pull requests without weakening the local gate.
- Have `ci.sh` post a commit status for the exact checked head SHA.
- Have `review.sh` publish the exact-head review verdict and findings to the
  corresponding GitHub PR.
- Make `github-sync.sh` a retry-hardened push for the standalone repository.
- Add shared configuration, retry, idempotency, and offline-fallback machinery
  rather than duplicating shell fragments across entry points.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, the affected protocol
  documents, and `EVOLUTION.md` so the normative text matches enforcement.
- Add deterministic tests using a fake `gh`; tests must not mutate GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- Online create/update paths are demonstrated against a fake `gh`, including
  local-to-GitHub number mapping and repeated invocation after ambiguous failure.
- Offline and unauthenticated paths preserve a usable local record, emit an
  actionable warning, and retain enough state for an explicit retry/reconciliation.
- CI and review publication is bound to the same head SHA as the local manifest
  and verdict; stale-head publication is rejected.
- Merge remains impossible without green same-head local CI and an acceptable
  same-head local review.
- Existing migrated records use the seed mapping without creating duplicates.
- The issue tree and script tests pass, and no workflow test performs a real
  network mutation.

## Reproduction / environment

At project handoff on 2026-08-31, the `github` remote points to
`git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git`. A `gh` binary exists under
`~/.local/bin`, but this main session initially had no `gh` on `PATH`, and
`gh auth status` reported no authenticated host. This is a required degraded
mode, not a reason to bypass the tracked adaptation.

## Initial classification

Applied by `local/bin/issue_new.py` (deterministic keyword pass, no model): `bug`, `ci`, `documentation`

### Data Model

Use flat optional frontmatter fields because the shell helpers operate on top-level scalars:

```yaml
github_repo: Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A
github_number: 7
github_database_id: 123456789
github_url: https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/7
github_sync: pending        # pending | synced | conflict
github_sync_reason: null
github_sync_updated_at: 2026-08-31T...
```

Local issue and PR numbers must never imply GitHub numbers: GitHub issues and PRs share one number namespace, while the local sequences are separate. Seed these fields from [github-migration-map.md](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md), rather than parsing that prose file during normal operation.

A record-level `github_sync` flag is only an aggregate. Add a durable, registry-owned operation journal, preferably one atomic sidecar per entity. Each operation needs a deterministic key, payload digest, prerequisites, state (`pending`, `applying`, `synced`, `superseded`, `conflict`), attempt count, remote object ID, timestamps, and classified last error. Keys should distinguish `issue.ensure`, `issue.parent`, `pr.head`, `pr.ensure`, `ci:<sha>:<context>`, `review:<sha>:<digest>`, and `merge.main:<merge-sha>`.

Define field ownership explicitly. Local records own workflow state, gate evidence, generated bodies, and desired labels; GitHub owns assigned identities and observed remote state. The brief does not define inbound synchronization for human edits made directly on GitHub. If those edits must update the offline registry, a separate explicit import policy is still needed.

### Idempotent Retry

Every command should commit the local mutation and pending operation before network access. Best-effort mode exits successfully with an actionable pending warning; required-online mode exits nonzero without rolling back local state.

Before creates, and after any ambiguous result, paginate the authoritative REST listing and match the stable local marker. Adopt one match, create on zero matches, and stop with `conflict` on multiple matches. Updates use GET, compare, PATCH, and verification. GitHub sub-issue attachment requires the child’s numeric database ID, not its issue number ([GitHub sub-issues API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues)).

Classify failures: retry timeouts, connection failures, `429`, and `5xx` with bounded exponential backoff; retain missing CLI, unauthenticated CLI, validation failures, and other permanent `4xx` responses as loud pending/conflict states. After an ambiguous status or review POST, query the exact SHA/context or marker/digest before retrying.

Commit statuses are append-only and interpreted by SHA plus context, so identical latest states should be suppressed ([GitHub commit-status API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/statuses?apiVersion=2022-11-28)).

### Empty-Branch PRs

The current `pr_open.py` can create a local record with an unresolved or null head. Preserve that behavior, but detect `base..head` having zero commits and record `pr.ensure` as pending with reason `waiting_for_head`. Do not push and do not manufacture a placeholder commit.

After the first real commit, reconciliation pushes only the feature ref, translates local issue footers through stored mappings, and creates or adopts the marked GitHub PR. Re-running `pr_open.py` currently allocates another local PR, so active branch uniqueness or an explicit “reuse existing record” check is also required.

### Same-Head Publication

- CI: publish `MIPStarRE/local-ci` only for the manifest’s SHA after verifying the complete manifest, `partial: false`, matching local record and branch tip, and remote commit existence. A mapped PR head mismatch leaves publication pending; it must never cause publication on the newer SHA.
- Review: require successful exact-SHA CI, exact-SHA lane files, a final local branch check, and `remote head == commit_id`. Always use `event=COMMENT`; the body reports the local verdict and unresolved count. GitHub authors cannot approve their own PRs ([GitHub review documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28)).
- Identical marker/digest publications are no-ops. A materially changed review on the same SHA receives a new auditable COMMENT review.
- Current race gaps: `ci.sh` does not recheck the branch tip before final success, and `review.sh` finally rechecks only `pr.md`’s `head_sha`, not the actual branch tip.

### Merge and Push Ordering

1. Parse and validate the exact manifest and review files inside `run_gate`.
2. Persist a merge intent containing base tip and reviewed head.
3. Perform the local `git merge --no-ff`.
4. Atomically record `state: merged`, `merged_commit`, and a pending main-push operation.
5. Push only `refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main` with ordinary fast-forward protection.
6. Resolve ambiguous pushes by querying remote `main`; retry only when it remains safely behind, and mark divergence as conflict.
7. Verify GitHub reports the PR merged through commit ancestry. Do not close it through the issue endpoint. GitHub documents that a locally merged branch pushed to the default branch can mark the PR merged ([GitHub merge documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/about-pull-request-merges?source=post_page---------------------------)).
8. Only then synchronize issue closures and permit remote feature-branch deletion. Local cleanup may proceed once recovery metadata is durable.

## Current behavior

The local lifecycle scripts create and mutate only the committed registries under
`issues/` and `prs/`. Local CI and review record their conclusions only in PR
frontmatter and per-head artifacts. The repository has moved to the standalone
`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A` GitHub repository, but the operative scripts and normative
protocols still describe a local-only surface.

The migration seed maps local issues `#0001`, `#0004`, `#0005`, and `#0006` to
GitHub issues `#1` through `#4`, and local PR `#0003` to GitHub PR `#5`; see
`results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md`. The owner decision is recorded in the
2026-08-31 re-hybridization entry of `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` and in
`HANDOFF.md` step 0.

## Expected behavior

GitHub is the ordinary issue and PR surface for track A. The lifecycle tools use
`gh` to create and update GitHub issues and pull requests, post local CI commit
statuses, and post local review verdicts. The committed local registry remains a
complete write-through record and permits work to continue during transient link,
CLI, or authentication failures.

The integration must be retry-hardened, idempotent under a retry after an
ambiguous failure, and explicit about unsynchronized operations. It must never
turn a missing `gh`, missing authentication, or network outage into silent success.
The local merge gate remains authoritative for CI/review eligibility and must not
push or merge a head that has not passed that gate.

## Scope

- Adapt `issue_new.py` and `issue_close.py` to create/close GitHub issues while
  preserving atomic local records and parent/child bookkeeping.
- Adapt `pr_open.py` and `pr_merge.py` to publish branches and create/update the
  corresponding GitHub pull requests without weakening the local gate.
- Have `ci.sh` post a commit status for the exact checked head SHA.
- Have `review.sh` publish the exact-head review verdict and findings to the
  corresponding GitHub PR.
- Make `github-sync.sh` a retry-hardened push for the standalone repository.
- Add shared configuration, retry, idempotency, and offline-fallback machinery
  rather than duplicating shell fragments across entry points.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, the affected protocol
  documents, and `EVOLUTION.md` so the normative text matches enforcement.
- Add deterministic tests using a fake `gh`; tests must not mutate GitHub.

## Acceptance criteria

- Online create/update paths are demonstrated against a fake `gh`, including
  local-to-GitHub number mapping and repeated invocation after ambiguous failure.
- Offline and unauthenticated paths preserve a usable local record, emit an
  actionable warning, and retain enough state for an explicit retry/reconciliation.
- CI and review publication is bound to the same head SHA as the local manifest
  and verdict; stale-head publication is rejected.
- Merge remains impossible without green same-head local CI and an acceptable
  same-head local review.
- Existing migrated records use the seed mapping without creating duplicates.
- The issue tree and script tests pass, and no workflow test performs a real
  network mutation.

It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\nrules.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation This file holds only\nMIPStarRE's project-local facts — it restates no shared rule, and shared\nrules never move here.\n\n## Style (MATHLIB_style)\n\n### Linter warnings\n\nDo not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add\nbroad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide\nblocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real\nmaintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.\n\nFix the warning at its source whenever possible:\n\n- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;\n- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass\n  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;\n- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;\n- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than\n  silencing `linter.flexible`.\n\nIf a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting\nexception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably\n`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.\nSuch exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as\nthe main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.\n\n## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)\n\n### Source-faithfulness checks\n\nFor this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean\nstatement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before\napplying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions\n`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed\nsource-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the\ncorresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.\n\nReject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,\nrepair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,\nor arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as\npositivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal\nencodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when\nmathematically load-bearing.\n\nReviewers should also inspect `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` links.  A source-labelled\nblueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction\ntheorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.\nAuxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the\nremark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.\n\n## Proof integrity (PROOF_INTEGRITY)\n\n### Companion document\n\n> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues\n> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check in the\n> lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference yet still\n> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,\n> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default\n> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).\n> Consult it alongside this file during review.\n\n### Project paper-realignment protocol\n\nThe canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions\n`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as\nfollows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in\n`AGENTS.md`):\n\n> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a\n> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`\n> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be\n> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The\n> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof\n> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the\n> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a\n> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or\n> conditional helper\n> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.\n> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge\n> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.\n\n### Axiom policy\n\nWhen an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,\nprefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`\ndeclaration, and add a regression check (for example a\n`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen\nthe axiomatic base.\n\nThis preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper\ntheorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a\ncaller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a\nproof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly\nconditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement\nfaithful to the paper.\n\n### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization\n\nThis is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or\ntheorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,\nmaking them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.\n\nSigns to watch for:\n\n- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,\n  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's\n  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)\n- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types\n  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions\n- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical\n  semantics (e.g., a \"projective measurement\" definition that does not enforce\n  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)\n- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be\n  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything\n- Definitions that \"work\" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to\n  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,\n  incompatible universes)\n\nWhen reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of\nthis?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the\nscaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks\nprogress rather than enabling it.\n\n### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift\n\nA theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker\nif its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.\nChanging a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\n\nThe most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an\nextra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional\ntheorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not\nrepair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named\n`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,\ngeneric `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those\nassumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.\n\nConditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet\nbe closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a\nnamed lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional\nhelper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named\nobligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show\nthat it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or\n`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled\nblueprint theorem with `\\leanok`.\n\nExisting bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs\nfor reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a\nstrengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the\nbridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is\nto restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a\ntracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.\n\nNot every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed\nto encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model\ninstances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be\nfaithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These\nconditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is\nmathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate\nstep of the source proof.\n\nFor every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Source-statement proof gaps\n\n**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read\n[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a\nproof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation\nstructure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why\nconditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a\ntracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.\n# Contributing to MIPStarRE\n\nThis document codifies the conventions for pull requests, issues, code review,\nLean style, and CI automation used in the MIPStarRE project.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Pull Request Conventions\n\n### Title format\n\nUse **conventional-commit** style:\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`, `blueprint`,\n`LDT/Pasting`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\nExamples:\n- `feat(LDT/SelfImprovement): add self-improvement induction step`\n- `fix(blueprint): resolve broken labels in chapter 7`\n- `refactor(LDT): extract shared preliminaries into Basic module`\n\n### Body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections. For mathematical changes, the body\nshould be readable by someone who has not seen the associated conversation:\ncite the paper or blueprint location, give the theorem label when one exists,\nand state the mathematical assertion precisely.\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this mathematical or documentation change is needed.\n- Cite the issue and, when applicable, the paper/blueprint file, line, and label.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed: definitions introduced, lemmas/theorems proved,\n  blueprint labels updated, and any deliberate difference from the paper statement.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how.\n- Examples: `lake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean`, `lake build MIPStarRE`,\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic.lean || true`.\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge)\nin the footer to link the relevant issue.\n\n### PR template\n\nA PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) auto-fills the\nMotivation / Description / Testing sections. Fill in the placeholders — do not\ndelete the headings.\n\n### Local hooks\n\nThe repository includes opt-in Git hooks for catching fast statement-integrity\nand blueprint-sync failures before they reach CI:\n\n```bash\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hook runs whitespace, the `scripts/tests` unit tests when any\n`scripts/**/*.py` or `scripts/tests/**` file is staged, the blueprint LaTeX\nconvention lint (`check_blueprint_latex.py`) when blueprint sources or the\nlint helper are staged, and the\npaper-gap-note structure and proof-debt audits on relevant staged files,\nincluding agent prompts and actions under `.github/`.  The pre-push hook\nchecks changed Lean files with `lake env lean`, repeats the fast\nstatement-integrity audits for relevant policy or prompt surfaces, and checks\nblueprint declaration synchronization when Lean or blueprint surfaces changed.\nThese hooks also reject explicit `axiom` and `constant` declarations in the LDT\ntree; use a tracked `sorry` for an unfinished source-faithful proof instead of\nturning the missing proof into a new ambient assumption.\nFor larger PRs, `MIPSTARRE_HOOK_FULL=1 git push` also runs the full local gate.\nUse `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` only for a one-off local-tooling bypass, and still\nreport the corresponding validation in the PR body.\n\n### Labels\n\nApply all relevant labels from the taxonomy in [Section 4](#4-label-taxonomy).\n\n---\n\n## 2. Issue Conventions\n\n### Issue templates\n\nThree issue templates are available in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`:\n\n| Template | When to use |\n|----------|-------------|\n| **Formalization Issue** | A specific theorem, definition, construction, or lemma to formalize |\n| **Bug Report** | Broken proof, type error, sorry regression, statement mismatch, or CI failure |\n| **Tracking Issue** | Umbrella issue for a chapter, theorem family, or proof stage, using GitHub sub-issues |\n\n### Formalization issues\n\nUse a descriptive, **bracket-free** title that names the mathematical content:\n\n```\nChapter 9 — finish the sandwich-chain corollaries in ComparisonLemmas\n```\n\nAvoid prefixes like `[Chapter 9] ...`: bot-generated branch names inherit those\ncharacters, and `]` breaks part of the PR automation stack. See\n[`pr_review_management.md`](pr_review_management.md) for the rationale.\n\nFor formalization issues, usually start with `formalization` + `2009.12982`,\nthen add the most specific live chapter or theorem-family labels that apply (for\nexample `ldt-basic`, `preliminaries`, `commutativity`, `pasting`,\n`main-induction`, `proof`, `proof-infra`, `statement-fix`,\n`sorry-elimination`, `mismatch`, `follow-up`, `blueprint`, or\n`blueprint-sync`). Documentation-only or tooling issues should use\n`documentation`, `ci`, `cleanup`, and/or `refactor` instead of\n`formalization`.\n\nWhen the work concerns content that exists only in the blueprint and not in\nthe original paper (arXiv:2009.12982), apply the `blueprint-only` label\nalongside the chapter or theorem-family labels.  Omit `blueprint-only` when the\nwork concerns a statement or definition that appears in the paper.  An issue\nmay need both `2009.12982` and `blueprint-only` when it spans paper-present\ncontent and blueprint-exclusive scaffolding or auxiliary lemmas; in that case\napply both labels so the scope is explicit.\n\nEvery formalization issue must give enough mathematical source information to\nmake the issue self-contained:\n\n- Paper source: a path under `references/ldt-paper/`, line number, theorem or\n  equation label when available, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.\n- Blueprint source: a path under `blueprint/src/chapter/`, line number, label,\n  and the matching `\\lean{...}` status when relevant.\n- Lean target: the expected declaration name and file path, if already known.\n- Dependencies: theorem labels, existing Lean declarations, and GitHub\n  sub-issues that must precede the statement.\n\nFor issues or PRs touching a source-labelled theorem, include a statement\nintegrity check.  List the paper assumptions, the Lean assumptions, the paper\nconclusion, the Lean conclusion, and a verdict: exact, faithful boundary\nhypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is\nstrongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a\ndocumented mathematical necessity.\nFaithful boundary hypotheses include formal domain data such as nonemptiness,\ndecidability, field-model instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator\nnonvanishing when these are implicit in the source.  Extra bridge, residual,\nrepair, or obligation-structure assumptions are not boundary hypotheses; they\nmake the Lean result conditional.  Do not attach them to a paper-facing theorem.\nIf they are unavoidable while preserving downstream proof work, quarantine them\nin a separately named conditional helper, cite the paper-gap note or tracking\nissue, name the obligation discharger that must remove them, and keep the source\ntheorem statement visible even if its proof contains a tracked `sorry`.\nFor the terminology used here, see the proof-gap protocol in\n[paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).\n\nDo not describe a mathematical issue only as a \"cleanup\", \"follow-up\", \"blocked\nitem\", or \"Phase N\" problem. State the theorem, lemma, definition, or mismatch\nin mathematical terms first; repository labels and scheduling details come\nafterward.\n\n### Multi-part work\n\nFor a chapter or theorem family spanning several PRs, use a title pattern that\nnames the mathematical region and create an umbrella **tracking issue**:\n\n```\nChapter 7 1/5: Self-improvement hypotheses\nChapter 7 2/5: Self-improvement conclusion\n...\n```\n\nAttach tracked issues as **GitHub sub-issues** of the umbrella issue so GitHub\nshows native progress, relationship navigation, and \"Tracked by #N\" links. The\nissue body can keep a short human-readable index, but markdown checkboxes and\nretired fenced tasklist blocks do not create native sub-issue relationships:\n\n```markdown\n### Sub-issues to attach\n- #101\n- #102\n- #103\n```\n\nUse the issue sidebar's **Add sub-issue** control, or the REST endpoint\n`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues`, to create the\nactual relationship. Put descriptions in the sub-issue titles or in prose above\nthe index.\n\n### Tracking issues\n\nUse the **Tracking Issue** template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/tracking-issue.yml`).\nLabel with `tracking`; add `chapter-tracking` for the long-lived chapter\noverview trackers. A tracking issue should begin by naming the mathematical\nobjective and citing the paper or blueprint labels that the child issues cover.\nThe `issue-automation` workflow will automatically:\n\n- Rely on GitHub's native sub-issue progress instead of editing body checkboxes.\n- Post progress comments on linked issues when PRs merge.\n- Suggest or create `follow-up` issues for genuine deferred work called out by merged PRs.\n\nThe repository does not currently use a live `all-resolved` label, so do not\nadd one manually.\n\n### Pinned issues\n\nThe three most active tracking issues are pinned to the top of the Issues tab.\nUpdate pins when priorities shift (`gh issue pin/unpin`). GitHub allows at most\n3 pinned issues.\n\n### Milestones\n\nUse milestones to group issues targeting a shared deadline (e.g., a paper\nsubmission or a toolchain bump). Assign a milestone when the issue has a concrete\ntarget date; remove it when the date no longer applies.\n\n### Discussions\n\nGitHub Discussions is enabled for design questions, proof strategy debates, and\ntopics that don't map to a single actionable issue. Use issues for concrete work\nitems; use discussions for open-ended conversations.\n\n### Blueprint sync issues\n\nWhen the LaTeX blueprint is out of sync with Lean code, open an issue with\nthe `blueprint-sync` label. Describe which chapter, theorem, or definition\nneeds `\\lean{}` / `\\leanok` tags.\n\nAutomated drift detection: the [blueprint ↔ Lean sync check][ci-sync] runs\non every PR and fails when a `\\leanok` tag sits on a Lean declaration whose\ntransitive axiom closure still depends on `sorryAx`. See\n[`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`][ci-sync] for what it checks and how to run it\nlocally.\n\n[ci-sync]: ci-blueprint-sync.md\n\n### Stale-issue audits\n\nIssues that cite specific `sorry` sites, file/line locations, or declaration\nnames drift out of date as `main` moves. Keep those citations precise rather\nthan replacing them with vague prose: update paths, line numbers, theorem labels,\nand short source paraphrases when the source moves. Before starting a new\nproof-closing round (or periodically as maintenance), run the audit script to\nlist open issues whose citations no longer resolve:\n\n```bash\ngh issue list --repo LionSR/MIPStarRE --state open --limit 500 \\\n  --json number,title,body,url,labels > /tmp/open-issues.json\npython3 scripts/audit_stale_issues.py --issues /tmp/open-issues.json\n```\n\nThe tool is report-only. Human review decides which flags warrant closing\nthe issue, updating its body, or dismissing as a false positive. A weekly\nread-only GitHub Actions wrapper runs the same export-and-audit sequence and\nuploads an artifact only when citations are flagged. See\n[`docs/stale_issue_audit.md`](stale_issue_audit.md) for the full workflow.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Commit Messages\n\n- Use **imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\").\n- Keep the subject under 72 characters.\n- When squash-merging a PR, the commit message should match the PR title format.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
